newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products dip except for high sulphur fuel.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products dip except for high sulphur fuel.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were generally easier on Thursday, high sulphur fuel the exception.

Gasoline was flat to weaker in a balanced market with a few sellers sniffing around for customers but not desperate to sell, while supply still remained on the low side due to continuing refinery maintenance.
Traders assessed prices for unleaded premium cargoes at quotes +$2.
Demand was seen out of Turkey which is holding a buy tender for two 25-30,000 tonne cargoes, and also out of Lebanon which is tendering for one cargo.
"There's not too much product being shown partly because of refinery turnarounds and partly because people are holding stuff back ahead of the tender results," one trader said.

Naphtha was flat to weaker as falling crude prices pressured prices, but the market was fairly tight. An Italian refiner looking for a cargo since before Easter was reported to be still looking around. Small parcels were available out of Turkey through an 18,000 tonne tender out of Aliaga, Greece and Libya.
The Eastern arb was likely to continue drawing Russian gas oil from the Black Sea and supporting premiums but weaker crude and gas oil futures hit prices by $3-4 a tonne.

Traders said Russian material was able to attract high fob quotes +$4 for large arb friendly cargoes although supplies of these were scarce before April 20. Non Russian 0.2 pct was pegged around high fob quotes +$3-4
High sulphur fuel oil was steady to firmer, boosted by aggressive quotes related bidding for pricing into recent Romanian demand and with local supplies fairly tight.
High sulphur cargoes were bid up to around $84 fob Med.
Low sulphur fuel oil markets remained balanced to weak with tight supplies countered by slack demand.
Cargoes valued around 50 cents lower at $105.50 cif Med.
